newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end slightly higher in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end slightly higher in slow trade.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed slightly higher on Wednesday, with many investors staying sidelined prior to Thursday's National Day holiday, brokers said.
The weighted index, staying within a narrow range all session, ended 2.95 points or 0.04 percent higher at 6,587.86.
Turnover was a slow T$38.25 billion.
The market, despite sound mid-term prospects, saw continued profit-taking following Saturday's rise to a 19-month high.
"Today, being right before a holiday, was not the best time for investors to start engaging again," said Lin Long-hsien of United Securities.
Brokers said the market largely was dictated by strong technical resistance established by Saturday's peak, and showed little reaction to news-based factors.

Electronics shares, boosted only slightly by a rise in the closely watched North American book-to-bill ratio, ended with a scant 0.16 percent gain. Acer Sertek soared the daily seven percent limit or T$3.50 to T$55.50.
"The sector has already risen a lot in the past month, so it was pretty indifferent to the b-to-b ratio rise," Lin said.
The market barely blinked after the government said it would not raise the business income tax in a streamlining reform.

The merging of personal and business income taxes amounted effectively to a tax cut, but still needs parliamentary approval before taking effect. A leak of the tax rate decision on October 3 triggered a small stock rally that day.
"The decision didn't come as a surprise to anyone, as it was revealed clearly in early October," Lin said.
The market is closed on Thursday for the national holiday.
Brokers expected consolidation to continue on Friday, forecasting trading in a 6,550-6,650 range.
